questions.stem: A reviewer is weighing competing claims about the sections of sonata form, among them "Recapitulation closes". Based only on the excerpt above, which answer is the one the evidence warrants?

answer.exemplar: Sonata form closes with the recapitulation, often followed by a coda.

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: recapitulation closes the form, sometimes with coda. On that basis "Sonata form closes with the recapitulation, often followed by a coda" is the supported choice.

questions.topic: How a listener hears the end of a movement

stimulus.body: The working note below records the evidence for a claim about how a listener hears the end of a movement. two cadential beats signal the end. A marginal reminder adds: two beats signal end. A reader must decide which of the four proposed statements the note warrants, without using outside knowledge.

questions.stem: The question turns on what the note above shows about how a listener hears the end of a movement. Given the proposal "Two beats signal end", which choice is consistent with the evidence in the passage?
questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: two cadential beats signal the end. On that basis "How a listener hears the end of a movement" is the supported choice.
